searchText: There is a typo, it should be [s - z]₂. <@427491045308235776> <@122421399213047814> I finished the implementation of `point_evaluation`. Benchmark number for all precompiles are included in https://github.com/ethereum/evmone/pull/979#issuecomment-2318808162. Also, it would be great if you could review the implementation (`kzg.cpp` file). are there hardware details for this bench? Intel Ultra 7 155U 4.0 GHz awesome thx how come EVMMAX add is so much slower than libff (4x) and scalar mul is actually as fast? can you run constantine benches on the same machine? ``` git clone https://github.com/mratsim/constantine cd constantine CC=clang nimble bench_eth_evm_precompiles ``` (assuming nim v2.0,8 and Clang are installed) This is quite bad machine for benchmarks 🙂 But I'll try tomorrow due to the 3 types of cores? I pin the benchmark to a performance core, but I also need to down-clock it from 4.5 to 4.0 GHz to keep the temperature stable. The evmmax is somehow PoC. No assembly, keep it simple. although there are some improvements in the pipeline. Specifically, we generated the field inversion using addchain tools, but it is relatively slow. libff in this context is using GMP. On the flip side there are high-level optimization missing in libff. They make pairings 2-4x faster than libff even without assembly.
